10 Jhonston St                                                                                       Commented [t1]: Johnston (wrong spelling)
Newtown

30.08.2019

Dear Ms Graham,

Re: Mr Barry Jones, aged 46 years

Dear Ms Graham,

Mr Jones is a forklift driver who sustained a work-related back injury three months ago. I am
writing to request a workplace assessment for him ahead of his return.

On 31.05.2019, Mr Jones presented with a four-day history of back pain, and a disc injury was
excluded via an X-ray. Over the following months, his condition has improved as the ROM has          Commented [t2]: x-ray (in small letters)
increased. However, pain and stiffness are still felt on back movement, and the pain worsens after
sitting or lying down for 20 – 30 minutes. Exercise tolerance has increased over time as he now
walks for 30 minutes a day despite finding it tiring. His current management plan includes
physiotherapy, naproxen for the inflammation, and carisoprodol for muscle relaxation and pain
relief.

After three months off work, Mr Jones is keen to resume his job duties which involve prolonged
sitting with occasional heavy lifting. He was advised to avoid lifting objects and to take regular
breaks. [Missing  patient is bored, discouraged, and restless]

I would be grateful if you could evaluate Mr Jones work environment for the appropriateness of his   Commented [t3]: Jones’
return and furtherly advise him on the duties he can perform. If you have any questions, please
contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
